title: Richard Diamond, Private Detective
paragraphs: Dick Powell stars as the quick-witted private eye Richard Diamond, whose murder cases combine hard-boiled detective plotting with humor, romance, and Diamond's habit of ending adventures at the piano.
Weekly private-detective series created/written chiefly by Blake Edwards around Dick Powell. The format deliberately combined Powell’s wisecracking tough-guy image with a recurring musical sign-off.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: NBC original run (April 24, 1949 to December 6, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], ABC original run (January 5, 1951 to June 27, 1952) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], and CBS repeat summer run (May 31, 1953 to September 20, 1953) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|dick-powell|Dick Powell]] (performer), Frank Worth (composer, conductor, and music director), [[person|virginia-gregg|Virginia Gregg]] (performer), Blake Edwards (writer, director, and editor), Wilms Herbert (performer), Ed Begley (performer), and Jaime del Valle (transcriber, director, and producer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].
The stories often return to Murder, Theft and robbery, Organized crime and racketeering, Blackmail, Kidnapping, and Explosives.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes network radio drama during the rise of television, Dick Powell’s musical-star to noir/detective persona, and Richard Diamond from live network series to repeat run during Powell’s television shift.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], and [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]].
